sources.title: World Tokens: Enhancing Embodied Policies with Training-Time World Modeling

synopsis: World Tokens makes a video-supervised representation the mandatory interface between a vision-language model and an action expert. Its current-context tokens support future-video denoising during training; deployment retains only the VLM, adapter, and action expert. Controlled LIBERO and physical R1 Pro results support improved control, with modest adapter overhead but substantial training cost.

problem.text: Image–text pretraining offers limited supervision for contact, occlusion, and displacement. Keeping a video model in the control loop adds latency; a parallel predictive loss can leave the policy free to bypass the supervised representation. World Tokens addresses both concerns through exclusive action conditioning on shared tokens.

contributions.text: A query-based World Adapter provides shared conditioning to a future-video denoiser and a separate action expert; the video branch is removable after training.

A Canny anchor supplies scene layout while encouraging the tokens to carry task-relevant visual information. Ablations favor combining video supervision, exclusive routing, learned queries, and edge conditioning.

inputs: Current multi-view RGB observations and a language instruction.
Training additionally uses demonstrated action chunks and eight-frame future RGB clips from the primary view.
outputs: An eight-action chunk from a conditional flow-matching expert.
During training, a separate video branch predicts denoising targets for future-video latents.

steps.name: Encode current context
steps.detail: Qwen3-VL-2B-Instruct encodes image patches and language into a variable-length sequence. World tokens summarize current context; they are neither predefined object slots nor predicted future states.

steps.name: Resample through a mandatory interface
steps.detail: The adapter uses 256 learned queries and 12 blocks of cross-attention to VLM features, query self-attention, and feed-forward updates. Width is 2048 with eight heads. The action expert has no direct VLM bypass.

steps.name: Supervise with future video
steps.detail: A projection maps the tokens into Cosmos Predict2.5-2B cross-attention context. A frozen VAE encodes demonstrated futures and the edge anchor. The denoiser receives noisy future latents and both conditions; its output is not an action-policy input.

training.text: Action flow matching regresses velocity from Gaussian noise toward demonstrations; video retains its native diffusion parameterization. Both losses update the VLM and adapter; video loss also updates its projection and denoiser.
The pretrained VLM and video denoiser are jointly fine-tuned. Adapter, projection, and DiT-B action expert start from scratch; the VAE stays frozen. World Tokens uses no embodied action pretraining.

inference.text: Each invocation recomputes tokens from observations and language, then generates eight actions using four flow-integration steps. Future targets, edge processing, VAE, projection, and video denoiser are removed. Feedback comes through subsequent observations; no online imagined rollout or inverse-dynamics extraction is used.

equations.expression: h_t=f_\phi(o_t,\ell),\quad q_t=b_\psi(h_t)\in\mathbb{R}^{K\times d},\quad a_t^H\sim g_\theta(\cdot\mid q_t)
equations.explanation: Equations (1) and (3): at step t, o_t denotes image views and ell the instruction. VLM f_phi produces h_t; adapter b_psi produces K tokens of width d. Expert g_theta generates the H-step action chunk solely conditioned on q_t. Here K=256 and H=8.

Equations (4)–(5) weight video denoising by 0.5. For actions, y is the target, epsilon standard Gaussian noise, tau uniform on [0,1], y_tau the interpolated input, and u_tau the target velocity. This linear path does not replace video diffusion.

results.setting: One policy trained on pooled Spatial/Object/Goal/Long demonstrations; 40 tasks, 50 evaluation episodes per task, 2,000 total.
results.comparison: Table 1 averages: StarVLA 97.8, World2Act 98.1, Cosmos Policy 98.5, DiT4DiT 98.6.
results.interpretation: Competitive simulated control without embodied action pretraining; not the highest overall average. Published methods differ in backbone and pretraining.

results.setting: Table 2 variants under the same LIBERO evaluation protocol.
results.comparison: Long: Qwen-GR00T 92.8; no world modeling 95.0; VLM bypass 94.1; parameter-matched FFN adapter 93.4; RGB anchor 91.5.
results.interpretation: Adapter-only improvement and additional video-supervision benefit are separable. Results favor exclusive query routing; training-seed uncertainty is unreported.

results.setting: Train jointly on BridgeV2 and Fractal real-robot data; evaluate in simulation. WidowX uses 24 prescribed object-pose configurations per task, averaged over configurations and seeds.
results.value: WidowX 71.5 average; Google Robot 82.1 average. WidowX block stacking: 32.0.
results.comparison: Published 4B Qwen-GR00T: 65.3 WidowX average; GR00T-N1.5: 57.0 stacking. Several Google averages omit Place.
results.interpretation: Highest listed averages, with task-coverage caveats. This published 4B baseline differs from the matched action-only baseline. Precise stacking remains weak.

results.setting: Physical right-arm control; lemon, strawberry, mango, banana; 24 trials each, 96 per policy, randomized layouts and policy order.
results.comparison: Matched Qwen-GR00T: 59.4 pooled; 54.2/58.3/75.0/50.0. Pretrained pi_0.5: 100.0 pooled.
results.interpretation: A 16.6-percentage-point increase over the matched system, with no mango gain. Pretrained pi_0.5 is contextual, not a matched training comparison.

results.task: Policy inference latency per eight-action chunk
results.setting: Batch one, two 224×224 views, 24 GB RTX 5090 D, CUDA-event steady-state median; excludes sensing, transport, execution, and server overhead.
results.metric: Median milliseconds per chunk (lower is better)
results.value: 61.85 at four compiled flow steps; 119.72 at ten uncompiled steps for a timing-only control.
results.comparison: pi_0.5: 56.32 at four compiled steps; Fast-WAM: 182 at ten uncompiled steps.
results.interpretation: VLA-level policy inference latency. Ten-step timing does not establish ten-step task success; it avoids overstating the architectural advantage over Fast-WAM.

limitations.text: Authors acknowledge considerable video-model training cost and a hand-designed Canny anchor. Broad cross-embodiment generality remains future work.

Success tables lack confidence intervals and training-seed dispersion. Attention entropy is descriptive: main-view means are 3.29 versus 5.22 bits over one episode per Long task, and adjacent steps are dependent. Sharper attention does not prove causal dynamics understanding.

Table 1 and Section 4.1 call non-pi_0.5 baseline latencies quoted; Appendix B describes re-timing Fast-WAM and DiT4DiT, with DiT4DiT on H100. This discrepancy remains unresolved. Cross-hardware entries and different horizons cannot establish controlled speedups.

R1 setup specifies cropped head-camera input, but rollout captions show head/wrist views; controller use of the wrist view is unclear. Figure A4 repeats lemon despite calling its tasks absent from the main figure. Selected examples cannot replace aggregate results.

reproduction.text: Use AdamW: beta=(0.9,0.95), epsilon/weight decay 1e-8, cosine decay, linear warmup. Learning rates: VLM 1e-5, denoiser 2e-5, new modules 1e-4. H100 training: LIBERO 70K steps/8 GPUs/batch 128; SIMPLER 140K/16/256; R1 30K/8/128. Matched baselines share steps and batch, not necessarily FLOPs.

Reproduce grayscale Canny thresholds 60/140, Gaussian blur sigma=2.5, and RGB replication. Explicit video resolution, future-frame sampling interval, warmup duration, action normalization, R1 demonstration count, software versions, and total training wall time are omitted and require clarification.

reasoning.text: Distinct VLM and action expert support Dual-system. Other mechanisms/Outside quadrants fits training-only video supervision: current-context tokens condition actions without deployed joint future/action prediction or inverse dynamics. WAM is the catalog’s broad umbrella. Latent prediction applies to video-VAE targets; no JEPA objective is used. The 2B label denotes the VLM backbone; the adapter adds approximately 0.5B.

discussionQuestions: Would the routing advantage persist across independent training seeds and equalized training FLOPs?
Does temporally aligned future supervision help more than static reconstruction with the same video branch?

evidence.location: PDF p. 1, title/author block and arXiv stamp
evidence.detail: Exact catalog title; Qu Tang, Benhui Zhuang, Bo Yuan, Xue Yu, Longteng Guo, Junlan Feng. Bo Yuan is corresponding author. Affiliations: JIUTIAN Research and Zhongguancun Academy. Stamp: arXiv:2608.09730v1 [cs.CV], 10 Aug 2026.

evidence.location: PDF pp. 1–2, Abstract and Section 1, paragraphs around Figure 1
evidence.detail: Motivation concerns temporal supervision, online video cost, and a policy bypass around auxiliary predictive features.

evidence.location: PDF p. 4, Figure 2/caption and final paragraph; pp. 5–6, Sections 3.1–3.4, Eqs. (1)–(3)
evidence.detail: Current images/language produce VLM features and query-resampled world tokens. Tokens exclusively condition actions and separately condition a training-only denoiser through projection. VAE is frozen; anchor is an encoded Canny image.

evidence.location: PDF p. 6, Section 3.5, Eqs. (4)–(5)
evidence.detail: Joint objective is action denoising plus 0.5 times video denoising. Action interpolation runs from Gaussian noise to target with velocity y minus noise; video retains native diffusion.

evidence.location: PDF p. 7, Section 3.5, Gradient paths, Initialization, Deployment
evidence.detail: Both losses update VLM/adapter. VLM/denoiser are fine-tuned, other learned modules start from scratch, VAE stays frozen. Deployment removes video components and uses four flow-integration steps.

evidence.location: PDF p. 8, Section 4.1, Implementation and Benchmarks
evidence.detail: Qwen3-VL-2B-Instruct, 256 queries, DiT-B, Cosmos Predict2.5-2B, eight-action/eight-frame horizons. LIBERO pools 40 tasks from four suites, each with 500 demonstrations, and evaluates 50 episodes per task.

evidence.location: PDF p. 7, Table 1, World Tokens and comparator rows, success and Emb. PT columns
evidence.detail: World Tokens: 99.6/98.8/97.4/97.0, mean 98.2, no embodied action pretraining. Averages: StarVLA 97.8, World2Act 98.1, Cosmos Policy 98.5, DiT4DiT 98.6; backbone/pretraining differ.

evidence.location: PDF p. 9, Table 2/caption; p. 10, Section 4.3, Mechanistic ablations and Structural-anchor comparison
evidence.detail: Long: 92.8 baseline, 95.0 no world modeling, 94.1 bypass, 93.4 FFN, 91.5 RGB, 97.0 full. FFN is parameter matched; edge anchor is inapplicable without video supervision. No uncertainty columns are supplied.

evidence.location: PDF pp. 9–10, Figure 3 and Section 4.3 Attention analysis; pp. 17–19, Appendix D and Figure A3
evidence.detail: Final-block attention averages 256 queries/eight heads over 8×8 spatial grids. Main-view entropy: 3.29 versus 5.22 bits over one episode per Long task. Displayed episode separates at all 32 control steps; authors caution that steps are dependent and statistics descriptive.

evidence.location: PDF p. 8, Section 4.1 Benchmarks; pp. 10–11, Section 4.4; p. 11, Table 3/caption
evidence.detail: BridgeV2/Fractal training precedes simulated VM evaluation. WidowX: 24 poses/task; World Tokens 74.0/85.0/32.0/95.0, mean 71.5. Google: 91.0/65.0/78.7/93.5, mean 82.1. Comparator averages may omit Place; dashes mean unavailable. Qwen-GR00T is a published 4B row here.

evidence.location: PDF p. 8, Section 4.1 R1 Pro setup/Baselines; pp. 11–12, Section 4.5 and Table 4/caption
evidence.detail: R1 right arm uses eight-dimensional joint/gripper actions and cropped head view. Four objects receive 24 trials each. World Tokens mean 76.0 versus matched Qwen-GR00T 59.4; per-object values and contextual pi_0.5 rows lack confidence intervals.

evidence.location: PDF p. 12, Section 5 Conclusion, final paragraph
evidence.detail: Authors identify considerable training-time cost and hand-designed anchor; joint training across larger robot datasets, embodiments, and tasks is future work.

evidence.location: PDF p. 15, Appendix A, Optimization
evidence.detail: AdamW beta=(0.9,0.95), epsilon=1e-8, weight decay=1e-8; cosine schedule and linear warmup. Rates: 1e-5 VLM, 2e-5 denoiser, 1e-4 new modules. Warmup duration/software versions are unspecified.

evidence.location: PDF p. 15, Appendix A, Structural anchor; p. 6, Section 3.4
evidence.detail: At video-branch resolution: grayscale, Canny thresholds 60/140, Gaussian sigma=2.5, RGB replication, frozen VAE encoding. Explicit resolution and future-frame sampling interval are not given.

evidence.location: PDF p. 15, Appendix A, Training scale; p. 8, Section 4.1
evidence.detail: H100, 16 samples/device, no accumulation: LIBERO 70K steps/batch 128/eight GPUs; SIMPLER 140K/256/sixteen; R1 30K/128/eight. Matched baseline steps/batches identical. R1 demonstration count and training wall time are absent.

evidence.location: PDF p. 15, Appendix A, Deployment footprint; pp. 16–17, Appendix B, World Adapter overhead
evidence.detail: Adapter: K=256, L=12, d=2048, eight heads, width-sized FFN, approximately 0.5B parameters. Appendix B attributes roughly 10 ms of 61.85 ms policy latency to it.

evidence.location: PDF pp. 15–17, Appendix B; p. 16, Figure A1
evidence.detail: Batch-one/two 224×224 views/eight-action horizon, CUDA-event steady-state median on 24 GB RTX 5090 D. Compiled four-step World Tokens/pi_0.5: 61.85/56.32 ms; uncompiled ten-step World Tokens/Fast-WAM: 119.72/182 ms. Ten steps is timing-only. Sensing, communication, execution and server costs are excluded.

evidence.location: PDF p. 7, Table 1 caption; p. 8, Section 4.1 Baselines and protocol; pp. 16–17, Appendix B Measurements/Comparability
evidence.detail: Main text calls latencies other than World Tokens/pi_0.5 quoted. Appendix describes running baseline code/weights for pi_0.5, Fast-WAM, DiT4DiT, the last on H100. Other entries differ in hardware/horizons; OpenVLA’s quoted value is for one action despite per-chunk table framing.

evidence.location: PDF pp. 17–18, Appendix C and Figure A2/caption
evidence.detail: Sixteen displayed frames sample an autoregressive video-branch rollout from one observation. It is qualitative video evidence from a discarded branch, not an executed robot trajectory.

evidence.location: PDF p. 11, Figure 4/caption; pp. 19–20, Appendix E and Figure A4/caption
evidence.detail: Figure 4 shows lemon/strawberry; A4 lemon/banana/mango with matched initial arrangements. Captions describe head/wrist initial views. A4 calls its three tasks absent from the main text although lemon repeats. Table 4 supplies aggregate outcomes.
